findings.rule: `.claude/rules/patterns.md` § Declared ecosystem capabilities: "Never reimplement or rename-wrap a declared package primitive." Reuse a primitive when its semantics match, and do not wrap it merely to rename it."
findings.wrong: Both sites inline `.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()`, which is the exact body of `collapseSpace` in the declared and installed `@orkestrel/html` — `node_modules/@orkestrel/html/dist/src/core/index.js:3603-3605` reads `function collapseSpace(value) { return value.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim() }` — a primitive helpers.ts:41-49 already imports from that same package, whose installed version is exactly the declared `^0.0.7` (node_modules/@orkestrel/html/package.json:3) and which the vendored `guides/html.md:588` documents as `collapseSpace('  a \n\t b  ') // 'a b'`, so the local copy is a duplicate of a primitive this repository already carries the guide for.
findings.repair: Add `collapseSpace` to the existing `@orkestrel/html` value import at helpers.ts:41-49, keeping the alphabetical order of that import list. At helpers.ts:2356-2360 replace the chain with `const value = collapseSpace(projectionToBlocks(projection).map(flattenText).join(' '))`. At helpers.ts:2548 replace with `const alt = collapseSpace(attributeOf(node, 'alt') ?? '')`. Do not touch helpers.ts:2387 in `projectHTMLLeaf`: that site collapses without trimming on purpose (its edge whitespace is a word boundary the later `trimInlines` owns), so `collapseSpace` is the wrong primitive there and substituting it would change projection output. findings.rule: `.claude/rules/tests.md` § Cross-cutting proofs: "Transcribe each flagship fence and assert the values its comments claim. Name resolution is not a behavioural proof, so a fence documenting a value the code contradicts passes every parity assertion. Change a fence, change the transcription beside it." The same file's table fixes the subject: "`tests/guides.test.ts` | Every documented API exists, every public API is documented, and every executable fence returns what the guide says it returns". `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity points to the same home: "That proof has a home: `tests/guides.test.ts` executes the flagship fences, per `.claude/rules/tests.md`."
findings.wrong: The file is the `@orkestrel/guide` name-parity drop-in and nothing else: it checks fence languages, surface membership, method tables, example presence, fence import names, and link resolution, and it never executes a fence or asserts a value a fence comment claims — so every behavioural sentence in `guides/markdown.md` (the `renderMarkdown` canonical forms, the round-trip anchor law, the depth-degrade semantics, the provenance rules, the sanitization floor widened by `src`) is unproven, and a fence whose comment the code contradicts passes the whole suite. No other test file in the package carries the proof either: `tests/src/core/*.test.ts` test the source directly and reference no guide fence, and the package has no `integration.test.ts`.
findings.repair: Add a `// ── Flagship fence transcriptions ───` section to tests/guides.test.ts below the parity loop, in the shape the fleet already uses at /home/user/fleet/contract/tests/guides.test.ts:289-360, /home/user/fleet/codec/tests/guides.test.ts:241+, and /home/user/fleet/process/tests/guides.test.ts:509+. For each flagship fence of `guides/markdown.md`, write one `it` that transcribes the fence's code verbatim against `@src/core` and asserts every value its `//` comments claim, and beside it a presence guard that reads the fence's lines out of `files['guides/markdown.md']` so the transcription cannot drift from the fence. Cover at minimum every fence whose comment claims a value, including the `scanLink`/`scanEmphasis` fence at guides/markdown.md:833-845, and the `renderMarkdown`, `renderHTML`, `htmlToMarkdown`, `span`, `fold`, and `stream` fences. Where a transcription disagrees with the code, stop and report it as a separate guide-drift finding rather than editing the assertion to match.

findings.rule: `.claude/rules/tests.md` § Test contract: "Measure an elapsed interval with `performance.now()`, never `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` returns whole milliseconds, so an interval built from two of its readings truncates at both ends and can under-report by a millisecond — enough to fail a boundary assertion against a timer that behaved correctly. `performance.now()` is monotonic and sub-millisecond, and it does not move when the wall clock does."
findings.wrong: The linear-time/no-ReDoS test builds its elapsed interval from two `Date.now()` readings (`const start = Date.now()` at line 624 and `expect(Date.now() - start).toBeLessThan(1000)` at line 626), so the measurement truncates at both ends and moves if the wall clock does.
findings.repair: Replace both readings with `performance.now()`: `const start = performance.now()` at parsers.test.ts:624 and `expect(performance.now() - start).toBeLessThan(1000)` at parsers.test.ts:626. Change nothing else in the test; the 1000 ms budget is a linear-time ceiling rather than a value one run produced, and re-deriving it is outside this repair.

findings.rule: `.claude/rules/tests.md` § Shared test infrastructure: "Data tables and case matrices belong in a setup file at any size; test registration does not." and "Test files import shared infrastructure rather than declaring local fixture factories."
findings.wrong: `VOID_TAGS`, `BLOCK_CASES`, `INLINE_CASES`, `OPTIONAL_CASES`, `CHAIN_CASES`, `PROJECTION_PARTS`, and `PROJECTION_CONSTRUCT_TAGS` are case matrices declared at module scope in a test file rather than in a setup module, together with the derivation helpers at lines 53-130.
